--dry-run inventory on up, build, down, uninstall and install
install and uninstall --name default to brain or brain-<id>

compatibility.down: before: after stopping its stack, downed every compose project holding agentibrain_* containers; now: stops only the selected stack
compatibility.uninstall: before: same whole-machine teardown and unlink of alias brain; now: stops only the selected stack and unlinks brain for the default brain or brain-<id> for a named one
compatibility.up, build, fix, install start (default b: before: downed every agentibrain_* project; now: replaces only owned legacy projects, refuses without --instance when two or more would be replaced, and still replaces a single other legacy stack because it holds the same fixed names (SV2-MUL-02 compatibility)
compatibility.named brains: unchanged from SV2-MUL-02 apart from explicit selection and per-instance alias
compatibility.no --instance: selection by AGENTIBRAIN_HOME and discovery as before

rollback: Run --dry-run first and select --instance default explicitly; reverting this commit restores the previous lifecycle. Config roots, volumes and vaults are never deleted by these commands. Rehearsed in CI by the default-brain tests; not rehearsed on a docker host.
limitations: Ownership reads containers named agentibrain_*; a differently named container carrying an owned project's compose label is still stopped with that project.
check, sync and logs are covered by settings resolution and the logs passthrough, not by a live brain-api.
Counters are per CLI process; persistence beyond the printed line is outside this package.
A tab after export in BRAIN_ID is not parsed; such a root refuses (fails closed).
